titre: ESAs publish Joint Advice on Information and Communication Technology risk management and cybersecurity
resume: The European Supervisory Authorities (ESAs) today published two pieces of Joint Advice in response to requests made by the European Commission in its March 2018 Fintech Action Plan: Joint Advice on the need for legislative improvements relating to Information and Communication Technology (ICT) risk management requirements in the European Union (EU) financial sector.

titre: FIA EPTA letter on the European Commission consultation on a digital operational resilience framework for financial services
resume: FIA EPTA appreciates the opportunity to respond and feed into the European Commission's consultation on improving resilience against cyberattacks for the financial services sector.

titre: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL on digital operational resilience for the financial sector and amending Regulations (EC) No 1060/2009, (EU) No 648/2012, (EU) No 600/2014 and (EU) No 909/2014
Digital Finance Package: Commission sets out new, ambitious approach to encourage responsible innovation to benefit consumers and businesses
resume: The European Commission has today adopted a new Digital Finance Package, including Digital Finance and Retail Payments Strategies, and legislative proposals on crypto-assets and digital resilience.

titre: Digital finance package: Council reaches agreement on MiCA and DORA
resume: The Council today adopted its position on two proposals that are part of the digital finance package: the 'Regulation on Markets in Crypto Assets' (MiCA) and the 'Digital Operational Resilience Act' (DORA). This agreement forms the Council's negotiating mandate for trilogue negotiations with the European Parliament.

titre: Digital finance: Provisional agreement reached on DORA
resume: Given the ever-increasing risks of cyber attacks, the EU is strengthening the IT security of financial entities such as banks, insurance companies and investment firms. Yesterday evening the Council presidency and the European Parliament reached a provisional agreement on the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).

titre: European Parliament approves agreement on 'DORA' regulation on operational resilience of financial sector to cyber risks
resume: On Thursday 10 November in plenary session, the European Parliament approved by a large majority the provisional agreement with the Council of the EU on the draft 'DORA' regulation on digital operational resilience.

titre: Digital finance: Council adopts Digital Operational Resilience Act
resume: Given the ever-increasing risks of cyber attacks, the EU is strengthening the IT security of financial entities such as banks, insurance companies and investment firms. Today the Council adopted the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) which will make sure the financial sector in Europe is able to stay resilient through a severe operational disruption.

titre: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector and amending Regulations (EC) No 1060/2009, (EU) No 648/2012, (EU) No 600/2014, (EU) No 909/2014 and (EU) 2016/1011
DORA in force from 16 January 2023 – check your digital operational resilience readiness
resume: DORA enters into force on 16 January 2023. Given the ever-increasing risk of cyberattacks, the EU has decided to strengthen the requirements surrounding the IT security of financial entities.

titre: ESAs publish first set of rules under DORA for ICT and third-party risk management and incident classification
resume: The three European Supervisory Authorities (EBA, EIOPA and ESMA – the ESAs) published today the first set of final draft technical standards under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) aimed at enhancing the digital operational resilience of the EU financial sector.

titre: EU financial entities cybersecurity upgrade: DORA is now alive and kicking
resume: The Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) becomes binding as of today for all financial entities across the EU. DORA is a harmonised and comprehensive regulatory framework on digital operational resilience.

titre: Publication de deux documents relatifs à l'entrée en vigueur de DORA
resume: Le règlement européen 2022/2554 du 14 décembre 2022 sur la résilience opérationnelle numérique du secteur financier DORA vient d'entrer en application ce 17 janvier 2025.

titre: Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions – A European strategy for data
Public consultation on the Data Act
resume: The objective of the Data Act is to propose measures to create a fair data economy by ensuring access to and use of data, including in business-to-business and business-to-government situations. The initiative would not alter data protection legislation and would seek to preserve incentives in data generation.

titre: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL on harmonised rules on fair access to and use of data (Data Act)
Data Act: Commission proposes measures for a fair and innovative data economy
resume: The Commission has proposed new rules on who can use and access data generated in the EU across all economic sectors. The Data Act will ensure fairness in the digital environment, stimulate a competitive data market, open opportunities for data-driven innovation and make data more accessible for all.

titre: Data Act: MEPs back new rules for fair access to and use of industrial data
resume: The 'Data Act' aims to boost innovation by removing barriers obstructing access by consumers and businesses to data.

titre: Data act: member states agree common position on fair access to and use of data
resume: With a view to making the EU a leader in our data-driven society, member states' representatives (Coreper) reached a common position ("negotiating mandate") allowing the Council to enter negotiations with the European Parliament on the proposed legislation regarding harmonised rules on fair access to and use of data (data act).

titre: Data act: Council and Parliament strike a deal on fair access to and use of data
resume: With a view to making the EU a leader in our data-driven society, the Council presidency and European parliament representatives reached a provisional agreement on a new regulation on harmonised rules on fair access to and use of data (data act).

titre: Council and European Parliament Reach Political Agreement on the Data Act
resume: On June 27, 2023, the Council and the European Parliament reached a Political Agreement on the Proposal for a Regulation on harmonized rules on fair access to and use of data (the "Data Act").

titre: Data Act: Council adopts new law on fair access to and use of data
resume: To make the EU a leader in our data-driven society, the Council adopted a new Regulation on harmonised rules on fair access to and use of data (Data Act). The data act puts obligations on manufacturers and service providers to let their users, be they companies or individuals, access and reuse the data generated by the use of their products or services.

titre: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2023 on harmonised rules on fair access to and use of data and amending Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 and Directive (EU) 2020/1828 (Data Act)
European Data Act enters into force, putting in place new rules for a fair and innovative data economy
resume: The new rules define the rights to access and use data generated in the EU across all economic sectors and will make it easier to share data, in particular industrial data.

titre: EU Data Act gives users control over data from connected devices
resume: The EU Data Act has started to apply in the EU, giving users control over data generated by their connected devices, like smartwatches and cars, while unlocking opportunities for small businesses to use this data to develop innovative after-sale services.

titre: Le Data Act européen devient applicable ce 12 septembre 2025
resume: Le règlement européen sur les données, ou Data Act, entre officiellement en application ce vendredi 12 septembre 2025 dans toute l'Union européenne.

titre: Evaluation of Directive 2008/114 on European Critical Infrastructures
resume: The European Commission published its long-awaited evaluation of Directive 2008/114 on the identification and designation of European Critical Infrastructures.

titre: EU Security Union Strategy: connecting the dots in a new security ecosystem
resume: Today, the European Commission sets out a new EU Security Union Strategy for the period 2020 to 2025. From combatting terrorism and organised crime, to preventing and detecting hybrid threats and increasing the resilience of our critical infrastructure, to promoting cybersecurity and fostering research and innovation, the strategy lays out the tools and measures to be developed over the next 5 years.

titre: New EU Cybersecurity Strategy and new rules to make physical and digital critical entities more resilient
resume: Today, the Commission and the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy are presenting a new EU Cybersecurity Strategy.

titre: Strengthening EU resilience: Council adopts negotiating mandate on the resilience of critical entities
EU resilience: Council presidency and European Parliament reach political agreement to strengthen the resilience of critical entities
resume: The Council presidency and the European Parliament reached a political agreement on the directive on the resilience of critical entities.

titre: MEPs approve new rules to protect essential infrastructure
resume: The European Parliament has given its final approval to rules on improving the protection of the EU's essential infrastructure. MEPs voted to confirm an agreement from negotiations with the Council on boosting critical infrastructure protection in the EU.

titre: EU resilience: Council adopts a directive to strengthen the resilience of critical entities
resume: The Council today adopted a directive and a recommendation which aim to reduce the vulnerabilities and strengthen the resilience of critical entities. Critical entities are entities providing essential services that are crucial for the maintenance of vital societal functions, economic activities, public health and safety, and the environment.

titre: Directive (EU) 2022/2557 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on the resilience of critical entities and repealing Council Directive 2008/114/EC
New stronger rules start to apply for the cyber and physical resilience of critical entities and networks
resume: Two key directives on critical and digital infrastructure have just entered into force and will strengthen the EU's resilience against online and offline threats, from cyberattacks to crime, risks to public health or natural disasters.

titre: "Mit unserem Gesetz zum Schutz kritischer Infrastrukturen machen wir Deutschland krisenfester!"
resume: Kabinett beschließt Entwurf zum KRITIS-Dachgesetz, das bundeseinheitliche Mindeststandards für den Schutz kritischer Infrastrukturen festlegt. Am 6. November 2024 hat das Bundeskabinett den Entwurf zum KRITIS-Dachgesetz (Gesetz zur Umsetzung der Richtlinie (EU) 2022/2557 und zur Stärkung der Resilienz kritischer Anlagen) beschlossen.

titre: KRITIS-Dachgesetz in Kraft getreten
resume: Am 16.03.2026 wurde das KRITIS-Dachgesetz im Bundesgesetzblatt verkündet und damit die CER-Richtlinie (EU) 2022/2557 in deutsches Recht umgesetzt.

titre: Cyberbeveiligingswet en Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten vanaf 15 augustus 2026 van kracht
resume: De Eerste Kamer heeft op 7 juli ingestemd met de Cyberbeveiligingswet (Cbw) en de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten (Wwke).

titre: Commission publishes evaluation reports on EU rules on machinery safety and product liability
Commission collects views on making liability rules fit for the digital age, Artificial Intelligence and circular economy
resume: The Commission has launched a public consultation on the rules on compensation for damage caused by defective products. A specific focus will be on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in products and services.

titre: New liability rules on products to protect consumers and foster innovation
resume: The Commission has adopted two proposals to adapt liability rules to the digital age, circular economy and the impact of global value chains.

titre: The Council adopts its negotiating mandate for a new EU law on liability for defective products
resume: The ambassadors of the EU member states agreed today on the Council's negotiating mandate for a new EU law on liability for defective products. Once finally adopted, the law will update decades-old civil liability rules and make them fit for the digital age and circular economy.

titre: Agreement between the Council and the European Parliament makes EU liability rules fit for the digital age and circular economy
resume: Negotiators from the Spanish presidency and the European Parliament have reached a political agreement on a new EU law on liability for defective products.

titre: EU brings product liability rules in line with digital age and circular economy
resume: Today the Council adopted a directive to update the EU's civil liability law. The new liability rules better take into account that nowadays many products have digital features and that the economy is becoming increasingly circular.

titre: Revised Product Liability Directive (introducing rules on strict liability for AI and other software) entered in the EU's statute book
resume: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 on liability for defective products was published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 18 November 2024. It brings software (including AI) into scope for the regime.

titre: EU adapts product liability rules to digital age and circular economy
resume: New product liability rules have entered into force, reflecting the increasing digital features of products and the growing circular economy.

titre: Besserer Schutz bei fehlerhaften Produkten – insbesondere bei fehlerhafter Software: BMJV legt Gesetzentwurf zur Modernisierung des Produkthaftungsrechts vor
resume: Wer durch ein fehlerhaftes Produkt einen Sachschaden oder eine Körperverletzung erleidet, soll es künftig in vielen Fällen einfacher haben, Schadensersatz vom Hersteller zu erlangen.

titre: Im Kabinett: Produkthaftung im Zeichen von Digitalisierung und KI
resume: Das Kabinett hat einen Entwurf zur Modernisierung des Produkthaftungsrechts beschlossen. Ziel ist es, die Produkthaftung an die Anforderungen der Digitalisierung anzupassen.

titre: Die neue Produkthaftung im Kontext von KI und digitalen Produkten
resume: Mit der neuen EU-Produkthaftungsrichtlinie und dem Regierungsentwurf zu ihrer deutschen Umsetzung (ProdHaftG-E) verschiebt sich die Haftungslandschaft für Software und KI-Systeme spürbar.

titre: New laws proposed to strengthen the UK's resilience from cyber attack
resume: Government is consulting on new measures to boost British businesses' cyber security after recent high profile attacks. New laws are needed to drive up security standards in outsourced IT services used by almost all UK businesses, the government says.

titre: Updated cyber security regulations proposed for managed services sector
resume: The Network and Information Systems regulations are to be updated to include MSPs and outsourcers, following a spate of supply chain attacks

titre: Cyber laws updated to boost UK's resilience against online attacks
resume: Outsourced IT providers will be brought into scope of cyber regulations to strengthen UK supply chains.

titre: UK Government Set to Introduce New Cyber Security and Resilience Bill
resume: The incoming British government has fired the first shot in its efforts to enhance the nation's cyber-resilience, with a new bill cited in the King's Speech on July 17.

titre: New legislation will help counter the cyber threat to our essential services
resume: The announcement of the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill is a landmark moment in tackling the growing threat to the UK's critical systems.

titre: New cyber laws to safeguard UK economy and secure long-term growth
resume: The government sets out the scope and ambition of the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill for the first time today.

titre: UK Government Sets Out Scope for Cyber Security and Resilience Bill
resume: On April 1, 2025, the UK government published the Cyber Security and Resilience Policy Statement, which details the UK government's legislative proposals for the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, originally announced in July 2024.

titre: Tough new laws to strengthen the UK's defences against cyber attacks on NHS, transport and energy
resume: Proposed new laws will strengthen cyber defences for essential public services like healthcare, drinking water providers, transport and energy.

titre: UK's Cyber Security and Resilience Bill makes Parliamentary debut
Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill: call for evidence
resume: Do you have relevant expertise and experience or a special interest in the Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill, which is currently passing through Parliament? If so, you can submit your views in writing to the House of Commons Public Bill Committee.

titre: Cyber Security Bill debated in the Lords
resume: Members of the House of Lords discussed the main principles of the Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill, during second reading on Tuesday 14 July.
